project.title: Plastic degrdation in Rhodococcus A34
project.projectDescription: The study aimed to explore the potential of bacterial biodegradation as a solution to the global problem of plastic pollution, specifically targeting polyethylene (PE), one of the most common types of plastic. The goals of the study were to isolate a bacterial strain capable of breaking down PE, identify the key enzymes responsible for the degradation process, and understand the metabolic pathways involved.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: The protein samples for proteomics were prepared using a modified protocol from a previous study. Cell pellets were re-suspended in lysis buffer, disrupted with a bead-beating method, and centrifuged to collect the supernatant. Proteins were precipitated overnight using trichloroacetic acid and collected by centrifugation. Protein pellets were washed with ice-cold acetone and resuspended in guanidine buffer. Protein concentrations were quantified using a BCA Protein Assay Kit. For proteomics assay preparation, 20 mg of protein was processed using the filter-aided sample preparation method and digested with a trypsin-LysC mixture. Peptide samples were purified using C18 Spin Columns and eluted in elution buffer. Tryptic peptides were separated using reverse phase XSelect CSH C18 2.5 um resin on an UltiMate 3000 RSLCnano system. Peptides were eluted using a 120 min gradient and ionized by electrospray, followed by mass spectrometric analysis on an Orbitrap Fusion Tribrid mass spectrometer.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: Mass spectrometry spectra were searched using Sipros Ensemble against a matched protein database constructed from the genome sequencing. Raw search results were filtered to achieve a 1% false-discovery rate (FDR) at the peptide level. Peptide identifications were assigned to proteins or protein groups following the parsimonious rule. A minimum of one unique peptide was required for each identified protein or protein group. Intensity-based label-free quantification of protein was performed using ProRata. The protein abundance was represented by the total peak height of all quantified unique peptides from one sample and was normalized by the mean across the entire dataset. Normalized proteomics data were further analyzed by protein function and corresponding pathways.
